name: Hugo Chávez
summary: Chávez promoted Bolivarian socialism through public control of strategic resources, social programmes and communal participation. He combined competitive elections and recall mechanisms with concentrated executive power, and pursued Latin American cooperation and a multipolar international order.

notes: His final election programme and October 2012 speech govern mature economic aims. Constitutional commitments are identified as such, while practice qualifies answers on executive checks and media. His oil expansion programme is recorded alongside climate rhetoric. Later policies under Nicolás Maduro are not attributed to Chávez. Pass of 2026-11-15 (claude-sonnet-5-5) searched his UN General Assembly speeches (1999, 2001, 2002, 2005, 2006, 2009), the Copenhagen speech, the Aló Presidente Teórico texts on communes (2009), the PSUV and the military doctrine, the 2011 annual message, the 2012 Golpe de Timón speech, the constitution as revised in 2009, the CRS report and Human Rights Watch 2008 for economy, government, world, ecology and society themes. Themes with no stated or recorded position of his stay null: sexuality and gender, abortion, drugs, technology, immigration and citizenship, most culture and religion questions, tax design and monetary rules. His El libro azul (1992) and the Aló Presidente transcripts were available locally but his speeches and the constitution already settled the answers given; Palabras de abril is an edited volume with other authors and was not used. Printed texts known to exist by him in the Project Gutenberg catalog, Miller Center and Voteview: none.
